# Design: Documentation and tests in the definition of done

## Context

The `spec-driven` schema (`assets/schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml`) is
embedded in the binary; each artifact instruction opens with the role block
introduced by `propose-review-roles`. The `propose`, `apply` and `configure`
workflows are Markdown bodies in `assets/workflows/`, rendered into
`.claude/skills/codev-<id>/SKILL.md` by `codev update`. They are prompts:
every line costs tokens on every run, and a line repeated in two places
drifts. `apply.md` already says "verify, then check off" (step 3d, the
"Verify before checking off" guardrail) but not which command runs the tests
nor that the whole suite runs at the end. `configure.md` caps its reading
at 5 docs and 8 source files and has no Bash beyond `codev`.

The init probe (`codev_core::detect::stack`) extracts the language, edition,
crate count and up to ten dependency names from the manifest; `codev init`
renders them into the generated `context:`.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Documentation and automated tests become explicit completion criteria of
  every plan written with the default schema, checked at planning time by
  `/codev-propose` and enforced at implementation time by `/codev-apply`.
- Test conventions come from the project first, from a short reference
  second.

**Non-Goals:**

- A machine check of these criteria in `codev validate`: they are guidance
  for the agent, like the rest of the role block.
- Recording the test framework in the init probe (see the last decision).
- Running tests from `/codev-configure`: it stays without general Bash.

## Decisions

### Decision: The criteria live in the tech lead's role block

The three new criteria are appended to the `tasks` "Done when" list, and the
`proposal` Impact guidance names documentation, in the same format as the
existing ones. The schema is where a project already redefines artifacts, so
a custom schema keeps its own definition of done. `/codev-propose` and
`/codev-update` both read these instructions, so both inherit the criteria.

**Alternatives considered**: putting the criteria in `propose.md` only (a
custom schema with no tests artifact would get them anyway, and
`/codev-update` would not see them); a project `rules:` default written by
`codev init` (only new projects would get it, and it duplicates the schema).

### Decision: Each skill adds only what it alone does

`propose.md` extends its existing traceability bullets — the scenario bullet
gains "names an automated test", one bullet covers documentation — instead
of a new step. `apply.md` amends steps 3c and 3d in place (tests after the
existing suite; the test command found from `context`/`rules`, manifest or
CI, never guessed) and adds one step before the final summary: run the full
suite once. The existing "verify before checking off" guardrail already
states the check-off rule, so no new guardrail is added. `configure.md`
adds testing rules to the `rules:` it drafts, a small allowance to read
existing tests within its budget, and the conventions reference.

This follows `_codev/decisions/0004-single-identity-for-skill-and-command.md`:
the existing skills are extended, no new skill is shipped.

**Alternatives considered**: a dedicated "testing" step in each skill
(repeats the role block and the guardrails, longer prompts for no new
behavior); a shared include file for the conventions (the workflow bodies
are self-contained `include_str!` assets and have no include mechanism).

### Decision: The conventions reference lives in `configure.md`, after the principle

The reference is a compact list, one or two lines per language (Rust,
TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Java), preceded by "the project's existing
practice wins". It is in `configure` because that is where rules are
written once and then reach every artifact through `codev instructions`;
`apply` reads `rules` and the existing suite, so it needs no copy.

**Alternatives considered**: the reference in `apply.md` (applied on every
task, but invisible to the plan and repeated at each run); in the schema
(it would apply to every project whatever its language).

### Decision: The stack probe is left unchanged

Recording the test framework in the detected context would change the
`init` golden outputs and the `init` spec for little gain: `/codev-configure`
reads the manifest and the existing tests anyway, and it is the step that
turns them into rules. The probe stays pure and its output stable
(`_codev/decisions/0001-functional-core-imperative-shell.md` is unaffected
either way).

**Alternatives considered**: parsing dev-dependencies for vitest, jest,
pytest and others in `stack.rs` (more parsing per manifest format, a new
field in the generated `context:`, and a second source of truth next to
the rules `configure` writes).

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Longer prompts cost tokens on every run] → Each skill gains a handful of
  lines; the reference is one line per language.
- [The full suite is slow on large projects] → It runs once, at the end of
  `apply`, not after each task; each task runs only the verification it
  cites.
- [The agent invents a test command] → `apply` names where to find it and
  asks the user when none is found.
- [A small change gets a documentation task it does not need] → The
  criterion accepts "the plan states none is affected".
- [Tests quoting the old instruction or skill text break] → The existing
  text is kept; only additions, asserted by new tests.

# Proposal: Documentation and tests in the definition of done

## Why

A plan is not complete if it leaves the documentation stale or the behavior
untested, whatever the project. Today the default workflow only asks each
task to name "its verification": nothing requires a documentation update or
an automated test, and nothing says tests must follow the conventions of the
project's language.

## What Changes

- The tech lead's "Done when" criteria of the `spec-driven` `tasks`
  instruction gain three items: the affected documentation is updated in a
  task (or the plan states none is affected); every spec scenario is covered
  by an automated test written in a task, a manual check only when
  automation is impossible and with the reason; tests follow the project's
  existing test suite, the conventions of its language, and its `rules`.
- The `proposal` instruction asks Impact to name the affected documentation.
- `/codev-propose`'s traceability check also verifies that a documentation
  task exists when Impact touches documented behavior, and that each
  scenario's covering task names an automated test.
- `/codev-apply` writes tests following the existing suite first, then the
  language's conventions and the project's `rules`; it finds the test command
  from the project instead of guessing, checks a task off only once its
  verification passes, and runs the full suite once before reporting the
  change as done.
- `/codev-configure` proposes testing rules for `tasks`, grounded in the
  project's existing tests, with a compact reference of mainstream
  conventions (Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Java) to fall back on
  when the project has no tests yet.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `skills` — the tech lead criteria of the default schema, the `propose`
  traceability check, and the `apply` verification and testing behavior.
- `configure` — testing rules among the proposed `rules:`.

### Removed Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- `assets/schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml` (`proposal` and `tasks`
  instructions), `assets/workflows/propose.md`, `apply.md` and
  `configure.md`; the regenerated skills under `.claude/skills/`.
- Tests asserting on instruction and skill text in `codev-engine` and
  `codev-agents`.
- Documentation, in `docs/en` and `docs/fr`: `skills.md` (propose, apply,
  configure), `workflow.md` (apply step), `reference/configuration.md`
  (testing rules example); CHANGELOG.
- No change to the CLI, the JSON contract, the file formats or the init
  probe. Plans written by custom schemas are unaffected.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The `configure` skill proposes testing rules grounded in the project's tests

In addition to the one or two rules it proposes for `tasks`, the
`configure` skill SHALL propose testing rules for the project's language:
the test framework, where tests live, how they are named and the commands
that run and check them. These rules MUST describe the practice of the
project's existing tests when there are any; the existing practice wins
over any general convention. Only when the project has no tests yet SHALL
the skill fall back on the mainstream conventions of the language, from a
reference it carries for at least Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go
and Java.

#### Scenario: Testing rules follow the existing tests

- **GIVEN** a TypeScript project whose `package.json` runs Jest and whose
  tests sit in `__tests__/` directories
- **WHEN** the user runs `/codev-configure`
- **THEN** the proposed `tasks` rules name Jest and `__tests__/`
- **AND** they do not recommend another runner

#### Scenario: Testing rules follow an existing pytest suite

- **GIVEN** a Python project whose tests already run with pytest and sit in
  `tests/`
- **WHEN** the user runs `/codev-configure`
- **THEN** the proposed `tasks` rules name pytest and `tests/`
- **AND** they do not recommend unittest

#### Scenario: A project without tests gets the language's conventions

- **GIVEN** a Go project with no `_test.go` file
- **WHEN** the user runs `/codev-configure`
- **THEN** the proposed `tasks` rules describe table-driven `_test.go`
  tests in the same package, run with `go test ./...` and checked with
  `go vet`

#### Scenario: The skill carries the conventions reference

- **GIVEN** the codev workflow catalog
- **WHEN** the `configure` workflow is resolved
- **THEN** its `body` states that the project's existing practice wins
- **AND** it carries conventions for Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go
  and Java

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: The default schema gives each artifact a role with "Done when" criteria

The instruction of each artifact of the embedded `spec-driven` schema, as
returned by `codev instructions <artifact> --json`, SHALL start with a role
block: a `Role:` line naming the role and what it owns, followed by a
`Done when:` list of checkable criteria. The roles are:

- `proposal` — product owner, owns why and what;
- `specs` — QA analyst, owns observable behavior;
- `design` — architect, owns how;
- `tasks` — tech lead, owns sequencing and verification.

The tech lead's criteria MUST require that the documentation affected by
the change is updated in a task, or that the plan states none is affected;
that every spec scenario is covered by an automated test written in a task,
a manual check being acceptable only when automation is impossible and with
the reason stated; and that tests follow the project's existing test suite,
the testing conventions of its language, and its `rules`. The `proposal`
instruction MUST ask the Impact section to name the affected documentation.

The rest of each instruction MUST stay as before. A custom schema's
instructions MUST be returned as written, without any role block added by
codev.

#### Scenario: The proposal instruction starts with the product owner role

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions proposal --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** `instruction` starts with `Role: product owner`
- **AND** it contains a `Done when:` list that includes marking every
  breaking change with **BREAKING**
- **AND** it asks the Impact section to name the affected documentation

#### Scenario: The tasks criteria cover every spec scenario

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions tasks --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** `instruction` starts with `Role: tech lead`
- **AND** its `Done when:` list requires every spec scenario to be covered
  by at least one task's verification

#### Scenario: The tasks criteria require documentation and automated tests

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions tasks --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** its `Done when:` list requires the affected documentation to be
  updated in a task, or the plan to state that none is affected
- **AND** it requires every spec scenario to be covered by an automated
  test, a manual check only when automation is impossible, with the reason
- **AND** it requires tests to follow the project's existing test suite,
  the conventions of its language and its `rules`

#### Scenario: A custom schema gets no role block

- **GIVEN** a change using a project schema whose artifact instruction has
  no role block
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions <artifact> --change <name>
  --json`
- **THEN** `instruction` is the schema's text, with no `Role:` line added

### Requirement: The `propose` skill checks traceability before presenting the plan

Once every required artifact is written and before showing the final
status, the `propose` skill SHALL re-read the artifacts from disk and check
that:

- every capability listed in the proposal has its spec file, and every spec
  file is listed in the proposal;
- every requirement has a nominal scenario and an error or edge-case
  scenario, or states why none applies;
- every scenario is covered by a task whose verification refers to it and
  names an automated test, or says why automation is impossible;
- a task updates the documentation when the proposal's Impact touches
  documented behavior, or the plan states that none is affected;
- every task names a concrete verification.

The skill MUST fix the gaps it finds directly in the artifacts. The check
MUST NOT modify any code file.

#### Scenario: A requirement without an error scenario gets one

- **GIVEN** a plan whose spec has a requirement with only a nominal scenario
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` reaches the traceability check
- **THEN** the requirement gains an error or edge-case scenario, or a stated
  reason why none applies
- **AND** a task's verification covers the new scenario

#### Scenario: A spec file missing from the proposal is listed

- **GIVEN** a plan with a spec file whose capability is not listed in the
  proposal
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` reaches the traceability check
- **THEN** the proposal lists the capability, or the spec file is removed
  if the capability is out of scope

#### Scenario: A plan without a documentation task gets one

- **GIVEN** a plan whose Impact changes a documented command and whose
  tasks update no documentation
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` reaches the traceability check
- **THEN** the tasks gain a documentation task, or the plan states why no
  documentation is affected

#### Scenario: A scenario verified only by hand gets an automated test

- **GIVEN** a plan whose only task covering a scenario is verified by a
  manual check, with no reason given
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` reaches the traceability check
- **THEN** the covering task names an automated test, or states why
  automation is impossible

#### Scenario: A complete plan is left unchanged

- **GIVEN** a plan where capabilities, spec files, scenarios, automated
  tests, documentation tasks and task verifications all cover each other
- **WHEN** `/codev-propose` reaches the traceability check
- **THEN** no artifact is modified by the check

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The `apply` skill tests by the project's conventions and verifies before checking off

When it implements a task, the `apply` skill SHALL write tests that follow
the project's existing test suite first, then the conventions of the
project's language and the project's `rules`. It MUST run the project's
test command, found from the project's `context` or `rules`, its manifest or
its CI configuration, and MUST NOT invent one. It MUST check a task off only
once the task's verification passes. Before reporting the change as done, it
MUST run the project's full test suite once and report a failure instead of
the completion summary.

#### Scenario: Tests follow the existing suite

- **GIVEN** a project whose tests live in a dedicated directory with a
  naming pattern
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` implements a task that adds behavior
- **THEN** the new tests are placed and named like the existing ones

#### Scenario: A failing verification keeps the task unchecked

- **GIVEN** a task whose cited test fails after implementation
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` verifies the task
- **THEN** the task stays `- [ ]` until the test passes

#### Scenario: The full suite runs before the change is reported done

- **GIVEN** a change whose tasks are all checked
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` finishes
- **THEN** it has run the project's full test suite once
- **AND** a failure is reported instead of the "ready to be archived"
  summary

#### Scenario: No test command can be found

- **GIVEN** a project whose `context`, `rules`, manifest and CI
  configuration name no test command
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` needs to run the tests
- **THEN** it asks the user for the command rather than guessing one

# Tasks

The skill scenarios describe what an agent does when it runs a skill; this
repository cannot run an agent in its test suite, so they are covered by
tests asserting that the skill body carries the instruction, as in
`propose-review-roles`.

## 1. Schema

- [x] 1.1 Append the documentation, automated-test and test-convention criteria to the `tasks` "Done when" list, and ask Impact to name the affected documentation in the `proposal` instruction, in `assets/schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml`, verified by the new tests `tasks_criteria_require_documentation_and_automated_tests` (covers "The tasks criteria require documentation and automated tests") and `proposal_impact_names_the_affected_documentation` (covers "The proposal instruction starts with the product owner role") in `codev-engine::instructions`, plus the existing `spec_driven_instructions_start_with_a_role_block` ("The tasks criteria cover every spec scenario"), `a_project_schema_instruction_is_returned_as_written` ("A custom schema gets no role block") and `the_embedded_schema_is_valid`

## 2. Skills

- [x] 2.1 `assets/workflows/propose.md`: extend the traceability bullets (automated test per scenario, documentation task), verified by the new test `propose_traceability_requires_automated_tests_and_documentation` in `codev-agents::workflows` (covers "A plan without a documentation task gets one", "A scenario verified only by hand gets an automated test", "A complete plan is left unchanged") and the existing `propose_body_carries_the_review_steps` ("A requirement without an error scenario gets one", "A spec file missing from the proposal is listed")
- [x] 2.2 `assets/workflows/apply.md`: tests after the existing suite, then the language and `rules`; the test command from `context`/`rules`, manifest or CI, asked when not found; the full suite once before the final summary, verified by the new test `apply_body_tests_by_the_project_conventions_and_runs_the_full_suite` (covers the four scenarios of the new `apply` requirement) and the existing `apply_is_in_the_catalog_with_the_right_tools`
- [x] 2.3 `assets/workflows/configure.md`: testing rules in the drafted `tasks` rules, reading existing tests within the budget, the conventions reference after "existing practice wins", verified by the new test `configure_body_carries_testing_rules_and_the_conventions_reference` (covers the three `configure` scenarios) and the existing `configure_is_in_the_catalog_with_the_right_tools`

## 3. Documentation

- [x] 3.1 `skills.md` (propose, apply, configure), `workflow.md` (apply step) and `reference/configuration.md` (testing rules example per language) in `docs/en` and `docs/fr`, verified by `both_languages_have_the_same_chapters`, `links_between_chapters_become_in_page_anchors` and an mdbook build of both books without warnings

## 4. Verification

I added the scenario **Testing rules follow an existing pytest suite** to the `configure` delta. It sits right after the Jest scenario in `_codev/changes/docs-and-tests-in-done/specs/configure/spec.md`, which is the only file I changed:

```
#### Scenario: Testing rules follow an existing pytest suite

- **GIVEN** a Python project whose tests already run with pytest and sit in
  `tests/`
- **WHEN** the user runs `/codev-configure`
- **THEN** the proposed `tasks` rules name pytest and `tests/`
- **AND** they do not recommend unittest
```

**Knock-on effect (reported, not applied):** task 2.3 in `tasks.md` still says the test `configure_body_carries_testing_rules_and_the_conventions_reference` "covers the three `configure` scenarios". The requirement now has four. That task is already checked off, so nothing yet guarantees that the `configure.md` body makes pytest beat unittest when a pytest suite exists. Suggested next step:
- run `/codev-update tasks` to reopen 2.3, or add a new task, so that test covers this scenario;
- then run `/codev-apply`.

**`codev validate docs-and-tests-in-done`:** 1 item validated, 2 findings, 0 errors. Both warnings are in `proposal.md` and predate this edit:
- `release_note_missing`: the proposal has no `## Release note` section.
- `domains_missing`: the proposal has no `## Domains` section.
